title: About two-thirds of duplicate '-R' vendor bills that came due were paid again, with no recovery visible: net 2,727,183.80 over 2016-2025, about 272,718.38 a year
conclusion: Observed, 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-29 (operating days up to 2520): 1,429 POs each carry a second vendor bill. Its invoice number is the first bill's number plus '-R', and its lines, freight and amount match the first bill exactly. These 1,429 are the only '-R' bills in the table. No invoice number is reused and no other suffix format exists. On all 944 stock POs among them, WMS shows receipts on a single day, with received qty equal to the PO qty. In no case does received qty equal two bills' qty, so the copy isn't a second delivery. Hartwell pays ordinary bills exactly on vendor terms (one lag per terms class). Every ordinary bill from 2016 to 2024 was paid. Of the 1,413 '-R' bills that had come due, 962 were paid (0.6808) and 451 (1,442,763.69) were held. 15 more (21,759.97) were not yet due at the end of the data. Counting all 963 paid seconds, 1 of which falls in the final 41 days, the net overpayment is 2,727,183.80, or 272,718.38 a year over 10 years. That is after allowing for 29 pairs where the first bill had been short-paid, so 5,102.58 of those second payments covered an unpaid balance. The paid rate is flat across amount bands (0.667-0.691), PO type (0.681 for both stock and special) and branch (chi-square 17.25 on 11 df, n=1,413, within chance). Vendor shares of duplicate dollars track vendor shares of all billing: the largest vendor has 0.3796 of paid duplicate dollars against 0.3761 of all billed dollars. Neither vendor credits (6.96% vs 6.94% chance) nor offsetting later short-payments (0.1308 vs 0.1331 chance) show recovery above chance. Interpretation (not observed): something in payables stops about a third of these copies, and the records don't show what or why. A rule matching a base invoice number plus '-R', or the same PO and amount, would have flagged all 1,429. The paid copies are candidates for reconciliation against vendor statements.

claims.text: 1,429 POs carry exactly two bills with one amount and two vendor invoice numbers. No PO has more than two bills (2016-2025).
Every second invoice number equals the first plus '-R', and the 1,429 second bills are the only '-R' bills. No vendor invoice number is reused and no other suffixed format exists.

All 1,429 pairs have identical bill lines (SKU, qty, unit cost) and identical freight. All 944 stock POs were received on a single day, with received qty equal to PO qty in 944 and equal to two bills' qty in 0. The 485 special POs have no receipts, so a second delivery can't be tested for them.

Ordinary bills are paid exactly on terms: lag 21 on 30-day terms (188,660 bills), 31 on 45-day (74,466) and 41 on 60-day (99,323). All ordinary bills in 2016-2024 were paid, and the only unpaid ones (5,235) are in 2025.

Of 1,413 matured second bills, 962 were paid (0.6808) and 451 (1,442,763.69) held. 15 (21,759.97) were not yet due at the end of the data. The 2025 matured rate is 0.6423 (n=137), so the low 2025 figure is partly an end-of-data effect.

Pair status: first full + second paid 934 (overpaid 2,670,334.82); first short + second paid 29 (56,848.98 net of 61,951.56 billed); first full + second unpaid 443; first short + second unpaid 19; both unpaid 4. Net overpayment on the 963 paid seconds is 2,727,183.80, or 272,718.38 a year, which is 5,102.58 below the gross figure.
Paid rate on matured seconds: 0.667-0.691 by amount band, 0.681 for both stock and special, 0.54-0.776 by branch, with chi-square 17.25 on 11 df (n=1,413), within chance.
Vendor 1 holds 0.3796 of paid duplicate dollars against 0.3761 of all billed dollars, at a duplicate rate of 0.0041. Its share reflects its size.

No recovery is visible. 6.96% of paid duplicates have a same-vendor credit within 1% of the amount within 250 days, against a 6.94% chance rate. None matches on both amount and SKU. 126 of 963 (0.1308) have a later same-vendor short-payment within 1% of the amount, against 2,396 of 18,004 (0.1331) ordinary sample bills.
Records with no anomaly: no payments without a bill, no non-positive payments, no orphan payments. Each second payment is a distinct payment row.

confidence: high that the copies were recorded as paid; medium that the money remains unrecovered, because statement and bank data are absent
not_evidence_of: Not evidence of vendor fraud or of any individual's fault, or of who entered or approved the bills (there is no user id). Not proof the cash is lost: recoveries could have been settled on vendor statements, by refund cheque or through netting outside finance_vendor_credits and bill-linked payments, and none of that is recorded. The tables also can't confirm that a recorded payment left the bank. For the 485 special POs, a second delivery can't be ruled out from WMS. The split between held and paid copies doesn't show that a specific control or person exists. The 12,026 short-paid bills (2,249,435.22) are a separate pattern and not part of this finding.
could_not_tell: Whether vendors refunded or offset the duplicates outside these tables (no statement or bank data). Who entered or approved each bill. Why about a third of matured copies were held, since nothing recorded (amount, branch, PO type, vendor, timing) predicts it. Whether special-PO copies reflect a second delivery.
next_step: Pull the 963 paid '-R' bills and reconcile them against vendor statements, ordering by dollars (vendor 1 first, because the dollars are concentrated there, not because its behaviour differs). Add an AP rule that blocks any bill on a PO that already has a bill for the same amount, or whose invoice number is an existing number plus '-R'. Review the 15 not-yet-due copies (21,759.97) before they are paid.
dead_ends: Second delivery: ruled out for all 944 stock POs (single receipt day, received qty = PO qty, never two bills' qty)
Recovery via vendor credits or later short-payment offsets: both at chance rates
Timing, amount, PO type, branch (chi-square within chance) and vendor do not explain which copies are held
System-copy artifact: the equal payment lag is explained by fixed vendor terms. No orphan or non-positive payments and no reused invoice numbers
response_to_challenge: Accepted all of the changes. (1) Size: I now use net overpayment, 2,727,183.80, or 272,718.38 a year, instead of gross 2,732,286.38, because in 29 pairs the first bill was short-paid (q148, q170). I re-derived this independently in q209 over the 963 paid seconds. q209 also confirms that the data ends on day 2520 (2025-12-29) and that 1 paid second falls in the last 41 days, which reconciles 963 paid overall with 962 matured paid. (2) Held vs pending: the old '466 held' becomes 451 matured held (1,442,763.69) plus 15 not yet due (21,759.97), based on the terms-fixed payment lags (q162, q184). (3) The low 2025 rate is partly an end-of-data effect (0.6423 matured, q170). (4) The largest vendor's 38% reflects its share of billing (0.3796 vs 0.3761, q167), so I reworded the next step. (5) Branch differences are within chance (q168). I added the challenger's supporting tests: single-day receipts equal to PO qty (q178), no offset recovery (q165), and no payment-record anomalies (q150, q175). I lowered confidence that the money is unrecovered to medium, because bank and statement data are absent. Nothing in the challenge needed rebutting.
